rca.title: CTBench fault-localization question #2
rca.question:
The question involves two major fault categories: route faults and port faults. Output format requirements: each line represents one fault; there must be no blank lines between lines; there must be no extra whitespace before, after, or inside each line; all symbols must use English characters.
Route fault output format: fault node;destination IP;fault root cause. Fault root causes include: (1) blackhole route; (2) missing static route; (3) incorrect static route; (4) ARP configuration error; (5) Layer 3 loop; (6) BGP configuration error; (7) OSPF configuration error; (8) loopback IP configuration conflict; (9) VXLAN configuration error; (10) L3VPN configuration error; (11) L2VPN configuration error; (12) ISIS configuration error; (13) SRV6-Policy tunnel planning error; (14) NAT external interface attribute misconfiguration or missing configuration; (15) NAT internal interface attribute misconfiguration or missing configuration; (16) global STP not enabled; (17) IP prefix list missing the corresponding user source IP address; (18) global VRRP hot standby redundancy protocol not enabled; (19) security policy rule does not permit the corresponding user. If multiple fault root causes exist, output each additional cause on a new line.
Port fault output format: fault node;fault port;fault root cause. Fault root causes include: (1) shutdown; (2) interface IP error; (3) traffic congestion occupying port bandwidth; (4) MAC address configuration error; (5) VPN configuration missing; (6) OSPF configuration error; (7) MTU value misconfiguration; (8) host information collection function missing; (9) interface VLAN configuration error; (10) NAT external interface attribute misconfiguration or missing configuration; (11) NAT internal interface attribute misconfiguration or missing configuration; (12) port STP not enabled. If multiple fault root causes exist, output each additional cause on a new line.
Be sure to provide the most specific fault root cause. Do not consider deploying NAT functions on Huawei firewalls in this question.
Route fault examples:
Test-Zone1-Spine-01;192.168.1.1;blackhole route
Core-Zone-Core-Switch-02;192.168.1.2;missing static route
Core-Zone-Core-Switch-02;192.168.1.2;ARP configuration error
Port fault examples:
Test-Zone1-Border-Leaf-01;GE1/0/1;shutdown
Test-Zone1-Server-Leaf-01;GE1/0/2;traffic congestion occupying port bandwidth
Test-Zone1-Server-Leaf-01;GE1/0/2;interface IP error
Core_SW_01 and Core_SW_02 corresponding Vlanif110 VRRP dual-master root cause.

path.title: CTBench path-restoration question #51 (source_question_id=117)
path.question: Path lookup from From Access-PC-01 to 10.1.1.20. Format requirements: connect nodes with the -> symbol; output the names of all nodes on the path (including L2 path nodes) and each node's physical egress interface name. Connect the node name and physical egress interface name with the '_' symbol. For the endpoint node of the path, output only the node name and do not output a physical egress interface name. The spelling of physical egress interface names must follow the interface names in the node configuration, such as the interface names displayed by the display current-configuration command on Huawei devices. Output one path per line, with no extra whitespace in the middle or at the beginning or end. If multiple paths exist, output each additional path on a new line.
